title: A map of the course
description: Understand the course as one connected journey, from inductive definitions to interpreters and type inference.

title: Your OCaml workbench
description: Use the official OCaml environment and build a repeatable study loop.

title: Thinking in constructors
description: Turn inductive rules into data types, recursive functions, and structural proofs.

title: Reading and writing OCaml
description: Expressions, types, pattern matching, currying, and algebraic data types.

title: The recursive way of thinking
description: Derive recursion from the shape of data and use functions to express reusable patterns.

title: From rules to an interpreter
description: Read semantic judgments and turn them into a small executable language.

title: What a function remembers
description: Explain lexical scope by drawing the environment captured at function creation.

title: Names, scope, and recursive calls
description: Connect recursive closures, mutual recursion, free variables, and nameless representations.

title: When evaluation changes memory
description: Separate environments from stores and trace call-by-value versus call-by-reference.

title: Following the pointers
description: Reason about shared fields, heap reachability, and memory safety.

title: The work left to do
description: Make pending computation explicit and see why raising an exception discards frames.

title: Objects as state plus dispatch
description: Build the mental model for fields, method lookup, self, super, and inheritance.

title: Reason before running
description: Use typing judgments to rule out classes of runtime mistakes.

title: Turn types into equations
description: Generate constraints, solve them with substitutions, and understand the occurs check.

title: One definition, many types
description: Generalize only independent type variables and instantiate a scheme freshly at each use.

title: When one type can stand for another
description: Understand substitution, function variance, and safe method overriding.

title: The small language underneath
description: Connect substitution, evaluation strategies, encodings, and fixed points.

title: Definitions → homework
description: Find the exact definitions, chapters, and source pages needed for each assignment.

title: HW1 · Learn to think recursively
description: Problem-by-problem strategies, connections, and boundary tests for functional programming.

title: HW2 · Build the ML− interpreter
description: A staged implementation guide for lists, closures, recursive procedures, and undefined semantics.

title: HW3 · Build the B interpreter
description: A memory-aware implementation guide for variables, records, loops, and parameter passing.

title: HW4 · Build the type checker
description: A precise design guide for a sound checker, including underspecified cases in the assignment.

title: Notation & glossary
description: Translate mathematical notation into the data and functions you implement in OCaml.

title: Course sources & reading list
description: All course PDF links, local download status, source discrepancies, and reading references.
